ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — David Hume — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review two weeks after completing adjuvant CAPOX and start of survivorship surveillance

text.paragraph: Review after completing adjuvant chemotherapy; start of surveillance. [S]

Mr. Hume returns two weeks after the last capecitabine dose of his fourth and final CAPOX cycle. The DPYD genotype before cycle 1 showed no decreased-function variant, and he received all four cycles on schedule at full dose. In cycle 2 he had three days of loose stools, controlled with loperamide. His September cold resolved without complications. Cold-triggered tingling after each oxaliplatin dose has left mild numbness of the fingertips and toe tips that does not interfere with buttoning, writing, or walking, and is not painful. He has no bowel bleeding or change in habit, no abdominal pain, cough, or bone pain. He walks 30 minutes a day and writes every morning. He feels well and asks what the follow-up will be. [S]

tr.td: Scars healed; soft; no mass or liver enlargement
Reduced light touch at the fingertips and toe tips; vibration slightly reduced at the toes; proprioception, strength, ankle reflexes, and Romberg normal

Adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon, suspected at presentation and confirmed by colonoscopic biopsy; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the documented 1775 bowel disorder and its retrospective interpretation as colon cancer

list.item:
Resected stage IIIB sigmoid adenocarcinoma, adjuvant therapy complete, no evidence of disease (C18.7). CEA 1.8 ng/mL, and no symptoms or signs of recurrence. Surveillance begins on the CMID colorectal cancer schedule. [S]
Written survivorship care plan given today: treatment summary, surveillance schedule, late effects, and whom to call.
History, examination, and CEA every three months for two years, then every six months to five years.
CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis in December, six months after surgery, then every 6 to 12 months for five years.
Colonoscopy one year after resection, in June.

Oxaliplatin-induced sensory neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Non-painful and not limiting function. It often improves over months, though some can persist. [S]
Check at every visit.
Duloxetine only if it becomes painful.
Protect the feet; check them daily.

Anemia, now mild and related to chemotherapy (D50.0). Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL and platelets 128, expected after oxaliplatin; iron was replete before chemotherapy. [S]
Repeat blood count with the January CEA.

Follow-up: Adult preventive visit later this month. CT in December. Surveillance visit with CEA and blood count in January. Next scheduled visit 1775-10-28: adult preventive visit. [S]
